title: Notification dispatcher core: events to channels
goal: A notification dispatcher core that turns domain events into CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD notifications, applies per-category channel routing, quiet hours, de-duplication and hourly email digests, and hands off to inbox, push and email channels.
scope_in: publish(event) entry point enqueueing onto BullMQ queue `notify.dispatch`; worker resolves recipients, loads preferences, builds the payload and writes the inbox row.
Payload builder producing exactly the CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD fields: id (ntf_), created_at, read_at, category, title_key, body_key, params, action, priority; keys follow `notif.<category>.title|body`.
Per-category param allow-lists: params may contain only prefixed ids, enums and integers (never free text, never anything from ct).
Default channel routing per contract (approval_needed -> inbox+push+os; billing_issue -> inbox+email; all other categories -> inbox), overridden by user preferences read through PreferencesPort.
Quiet hours: suppress `push` and `os`, never for security_alert or billing_issue; high-priority approval_needed bypasses only if the user opted in.
De-duplication by (user, dedupe_key) over 10 min; hourly email digest job batching low/normal items for users with email enabled.
Notification table and ports to channel senders (PushSenderPort, EmailPort) so B064 and the email service plug in.
scope_out: Inbox REST endpoints: B065. Preference storage, validation and endpoints: B066.
Producing events (approvals, billing, usage): each producing lane calls publish().
The client-local `os` channel (clients render it themselves from inbox/push).
build_against: In-memory Redis/BullMQ test mode from B009, fake PreferencesPort, PushSenderPort and EmailPort recorders, injected clock. Payload fixtures validated against the generated notification type.
interfaces: NotificationEvent = {category: NotifCategory, recipients: {users: UserId[]} | {workspace: WorkspaceId, roles: WorkspaceRole[]} | {session: SessionId, members: MemberId[]}, params: Record<string,string|number>, priority?: 'low'|'normal'|'high', dedupeKey?: string, action?: {type: string, deeplink: string}}
decideChannels(input:{category, priority, prefs: UserNotificationPrefs, quiet: boolean}): Set<'inbox'|'push'|'email'|'os'>
Ports: PreferencesPort.get(userId); QuietHoursPort.isQuiet(prefs, now); PushSenderPort.enqueue(userId, payload); EmailPort.enqueue(userId, template, payload)
Table notification(id pk 'ntf_', user_id, category, params jsonb, priority, action jsonb, dedupe_key, created_at, read_at, unique(user_id, dedupe_key) where dedupe_key not null)
acceptance: publish of approval_needed to one user with default prefs creates one inbox row and one PushSenderPort.enqueue call; billing_issue creates inbox + one EmailPort.enqueue and no push; mention creates inbox only.
The stored/returned payload validates against the generated notification type and contains no keys outside the CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD set; title_key equals 'notif.approval_needed.title'.

An event whose params contain a free-text string (e.g. a value with a space or longer than 64 chars) or a key not in the category allow-list is rejected at publish with a typed error and nothing is written.
With quiet hours active, approval_needed (normal priority) yields inbox only; with priority high and opt-in yields push; security_alert and billing_issue ignore quiet hours.
Two events with the same (user, dedupeKey) within 10 min produce one row; after 10 min a second row is created.
Recipient resolution by {workspace, roles:['owner','admin']} returns only active members with those roles, never members who left.

The hourly digest job sends one email per user containing all unsent low/normal email-channel items from the last hour (max 50 per email), marks them sent, and sends nothing when there are none; running it twice in the same hour sends nothing the second time.
Dispatch failure in the push channel does not prevent the inbox row (channels are isolated; test with a throwing PushSenderPort).
Queue job failures retry 5 times with exponential backoff plus jitter then land in dead-letter queue notify.dispatch.dlq.
tests: dispatcher.routing.test.ts: matrix of category x priority x quiet x prefs
dispatcher.params.test.ts: allow-list and rejection of free text
dispatcher.digest.test.ts: batching and idempotent hourly run
dispatcher.isolation.test.ts: channel failure isolation and DLQ
guardrails: MUST NOT put display text in a payload; only keys, ids, enums and integers (CT-NOTIF-PAYLOAD).
MUST NOT accept anything derived from ct or plaintext work content as a param, and MUST NOT log params values beyond category and counts.
MUST NOT suppress security_alert or billing_issue by quiet hours or by disabling the channel `inbox`.
MUST NOT notify a user who is not a member of the related workspace/session at publish time.
Jobs MUST be idempotent: re-running a dispatch job for the same event id cannot create a second inbox row (dedupe by event id).
failure_modes: Preferences read fails -> fall back to contract defaults for that category and log a warning; never drop security_alert or billing_issue.
Email provider down -> email jobs retry with backoff up to 24 h, then dead-letter; inbox unaffected.
Redis unavailable at publish -> publish throws a typed retryable error; the producing lane decides (outbox) and must not lose the event silently.
